problems: bf16-window control is not one number: 0.4102 (results/fast_checks/F04.log:42, host-launch timed), 0.3821 (fast_checks/bench_triton_graphtimed.txt:42), 0.3815 (fast_checks_v2/F04.log:42), 0.3817 (fast_checks_final/F04.log:45), g3 per-run 0.3815-0.3822 (means 0.3817 in the adopted and v9 processes, 0.3820 in the v8 processes), g3-final per-run 0.3816-0.3823 (mean 0.3819), 0.3791/0.3786 with bench_kernel.py complete windows (run-quick-einstein-v5 and gpu-suite e_full_cycles_bf16*.log:27), and the hard-coded 0.38/0.382 of summary.txt and docs/DECISIONS.md:14 (G3 threshold 0.306 = 0.8 x 0.382). Within the graph-timed harness the spread is about 0.2%; across harnesses about 8%.

Mixed experiments in one pairing: '0.3004 vs 0.3817 in results/g3-final' does not exist. 0.3817 is results/g3 (n=6, G3.txt:4); g3-final's v9 control is 0.3819 (G3.txt:3). PLAN6_BACKLOG.md:208 (G3 row) says 'MET (14 Nov 13:08)', the time of results/g3, but quotes g3-final's interval (1.270-1.272, 10 runs); B54 (line 251) and DECISIONS.md 'Changes' (6 paired runs) cite g3.

The G3 verdict depends on a run-order effect in the fold timing. The same fold binary (build_v9 libleapquant_fastfold.so 8a78d45fa72cbc8b) times 0.989-1.081 ms (mean 1.034 g3 / 1.036 g3-final) in the adopted processes, after the Triton decode, but 0.946-0.955 ms (mean 0.950) after the CUDA v8/v9 decode, in the same interleaved sessions. With the adopted-arm fold, v9 = 0.2410 + 1.036/16 = 0.3058 ms per token, ratio 1.249 against 0.3819, below the 1.25 gate. summary.txt:693-695 acknowledges that 'the fold time moves with what ran before it'. The same pattern appears in fast_decode_v5 (1.037-1.072 vs 0.975-0.982 ms) and fast_decode_v7 (v6 fold 1.093-1.097 vs 0.980-0.985 ms).

Timing is asymmetric inside kernel/bench_triton.py (gpu_ms). The LeapQuant decode and the SGLang packed kernels are timed as 10 back-to-back calls per CUDA graph (median of 20 replays / 10). Each SGLang window position (before=restore_state, so calls=1) and the fold are timed as 1 call per graph, and the fold takes the median of only 5 replays. The report text ('Every kernel timed the same way: ten calls captured in a CUDA graph, the median of 20 replays'; reports/generate_reports.py:596-599, the same in the snapshot) is wrong. The same bf16 window kernel gives 0.3791 when timed as back-to-back complete windows and 0.3815-0.3823 as single-call graph replays.

Host-launch-timed and graph-timed numbers are mixed. summary.txt:264-271 (0.493 vs 0.410, '0.83x') comes from fast_checks/F04.log, before the timing fix. summary.txt:326-331 (0.3997 vs 0.3821, '0.96x') comes from the graph-timed file. The step from 0.4929 to 0.3997 combines three changes: about 30 us per launch of removed launch time (window bf16 0.4102 to 0.3821, packed fp32 1.2282 to 1.1980), a decode retune (0.3406 to 0.2524) and a fold change (2.437 to 2.356). The exact-kernel charts (kernel_per_step/append/fold_*.png) use bench_kernel.py wall clock including Python launch, and kernel.html of the v7_2250 and v7_2304 reports puts both harnesses on one page. The same exact-kernel fold measured 9.784 ms in profile_kernel.py (run-quick-einstein-v4/profile_final_b512.txt:24, the summary's '9.78') and 10.52 ms in bench_kernel.py (run-quick-einstein-v4/e_kernel_speed_bf16.log:18).

Copied measurements: run-quick-einstein-v6/e_triton_speed.txt and run-quick-einstein-v7/e_triton_speed.txt are byte copies of fast_checks/bench_triton_graphtimed.txt. That one run was measured after round 6 had finished, with a retuned decode (0.25 instead of the 0.34 ms its servers ran), so the round-6 kernel page does not show round 6's kernel. The round-7 page also does not show round 7's own check (fast_checks_v2/F04.log: 0.3980 / 0.3815). run-quick-einstein-v5/e_kernel_speed_{bf16,fp32}.log are byte copies of v4's, made at 11:46:04 local (same libleapquant_cuda.so 8f89426f2c9f9e15). The reuse is disclosed only in NOTES.txt and serving.html, not on kernel.html.

The snapshot's kernel charts predate the later kernels. The only per-token chart in reports.zip, img/kernel_triton_per_token.png (in v6_2004, v7_2109, v7_2250 and v7_2304), shows the Triton-fold/Triton-decode run of 03:56 UTC. No report page shows the CUDA fold v1-v6, the batched-GS fold, the CUDA decodes v5/v7/v8/v9 or G3. Reports from round 9 on have no kernel.html, and round11 lists results/g3 as a source, but parse_triton_speed reads only e_triton_speed*.txt. The kernel pages of v7_2250, v7_2304, v8-radix_2328 and gpu-suite_2037 show the EXACT CUDA kernel (gpu-suite T11, fold 10.52 ms at 512), not the fast kernels those rounds served. The top-level reports/kernel.html (13 Nov 00:39) shows the old machine's 5.31 ms/step kernel, and all_reports.html links it as 'here'.

Provenance gaps: fast_checks, fast_checks_v2, fast_checks_final, fast_fold_v2, fast_fold_v3, fast_experiments, exact_v2, gpu-suite, run-quick-einstein(-v6, -v7) and ncu_v7/v9 have no manifest. The manifests of fast_fold_v1/v4/v6 and fast_decode_v5/v7 lack the CUDA fold/decode library hash, build_dir and CUDA sources (summary.txt:706-710). g3's fast_cuda_source_hash 6ab61a43fe988cda equals build_v8's, so it hashes stale tree sources (summary.txt:791-795). The g3 and g3-final environment lines say decode=triton with no variant. The build_v9 decode source (md5 95926011...) is not in the repository: kernel/leapquant_fast_decode.cu now has md5 02b74144dc04597f8f3406a9bffc1153 (variant 10 added later), and no *_v6only or *_v8only copies or .so libraries are present. Only the fold source (md5 e16651c1...) still matches.

Same arm label, different binaries. 'LeapQuant per token' moves 0.4929 -> 0.3997 -> 0.3980 -> 0.3969 -> 0.3323 -> ~0.322 -> 0.3193 -> 0.3171 -> 0.3056 -> 0.3004 across the Triton fold, CUDA fold v1/v3/v4/v6, batched GS and the Triton (pre/post retune) and CUDA v5/v7/v8/v9 decodes. G3's 'adopted' arm uses ~/lqdec7/build_v9's library, not the main serving runs' ~/lqfold4/build_v6 library (round 10: 14e826957ec07569; openloop on: ae3affd2cce95d37, per results/QUEUE.txt).

Cross-session ratios in prose: '0.401 -> 0.332 ms = 1.15x faster than bf16 window (0.382)' (summary.txt:509-510; fast_fold_v1 timed no SGLang kernel), '0.322 ms = 1.19x' (summary.txt:609), '0.320 = 1.19x' (PLAN6 B01), '0.306 = exactly the G3 limit' (summary.txt:744) and '~0.316' / '~0.302' (summary.txt:698-699) each divide a LeapQuant time from one run by a control from another session. B01's '1.04-1.14 ms (v3/v4)' has no v3/v4 raw value at 1.04 (minimum 1.104 in v3 and 1.076 in v4; 1.037 occurs only in fast_decode_v5/bench_decode_triton_2.txt:31).

Grid and repetition gaps. CUDA v9 has timings at batch 512 only (g3/g3-final). No v9 timing exists at batch 32 or 128: fast_decode_v9 has no bench files, and its 'worst 3.9e-5 (batch 4)' line comes from memcheck.txt, run under compute-sanitizer. The historical Triton per-token values are single runs (n=1 per batch). All kernel timings use synthetic random states with every row folding on the same step (aligned folds); staggered folds were not benchmarked (B04 open). fast_decode_v9 holds only 5 of the 9 trace verifications that summary.txt:796 cites, and no verify_summary/engine/restore files (relevant to topic 7).

Nsight numbers are taken at locked clocks of about 1.04-1.06 GHz: v9 decode 249.47 us and batched-GS fold 1.42 ms (ncu_v9), Triton decode 305.22 us (fast_fold_v4/ncu_decode.txt:12), v7 decode 704.83 us. They cannot be plotted against bench_triton times (v9 decode 0.2410 ms, fold 0.950 ms).

Ratio conventions differ. G3.txt's ratio is the mean of per-run (bf16 window / LeapQuant) with a t-interval, and the gate is >= 1.25 (= LeapQuant at least 20% below). The summary's '~3.99x vs SGLang fp32 packed (1.198 ms)' and the report's 'vs packed' labels are ratios of means computed in prose or HTML, not stored in any results file.

problems: ROWS COPIED BETWEEN ROUNDS: results/run-quick-einstein-v3, -v4, -v5 config1_fp32/config2_fp32_window/config3_bf16_window logs (12 files each) are byte-identical (md5) to run-quick-einstein-v2's; only config4_leapquant was re-measured in rounds 3-5 (disclosed only in each NOTES.txt). Any figure showing 'round 3/4/5 baselines' plots round 2's numbers (1394.6 / 2716.9 / 3850.4 / 4049.5 fp32 etc.).

ROUND 11 HAS NO fp32 ARM: the 'vs round 10's fp32' ratios (summary.txt:800-808, up to 1.41x) divide a round-11 LeapQuant (build_v9, CUDA decode v9, step reuse) by a round-10 fp32 run from another session. The snapshot report reports/round11_20261114-0545 was generated 'from results/round11, results/round10, results/g3' and generate_reports.find() lets the run's own folder hide same-named files, so for points round 11 did not run (aa1k c4, c128; ix8k1k c1, c16, c64) the 'bf16 window' and 'LeapQuant' cells are ROUND 10's logs under the same labels (off_*_r1): the paired table and its sweep chart mix two sessions and two LeapQuant binaries (build_v6 original 14e82695 + Triton decode vs build_v9 + v9 decode).

SAME ARM LABEL, DIFFERENT BINARIES: 'leapquant'/'leapquant_cuda'/'config4_leapquant' covers phase-1 exact kernel (rounds 1-5, gpu-suite), Triton compressed (v6-v8), pre-v3 CUDA fold of unknown binary (round 9), build_v6 v6-original fold 14e82695 + Triton decode (round 10), build_v6 batched-GS ae3affd2 + Triton decode (openloop, round9-equalmem, sglang-best; swapped in place mid-queue at 11:20Z per results/QUEUE.txt), build_v9 8a78d45f + CUDA decode v9 + step reuse (round 11 on), ~/lqdec8 fused slot copy (ab-slotcopy).

BUILD NOT IDENTIFIED: rounds 1, 6, 7, 8 have no manifest; round 9/10 manifests have no fast-fold library hash; v2's 'manifest_written_after_the_run.txt' records libleapquant_cuda.so built 18:55:31Z, after the round-2 LeapQuant server ran (18:28-18:35Z). Manifest 'environment' lines are written once per run before the arms export LEAPQUANT_STATE/ALIGN_FOLDS/FOLD_POLICY, so they show the outer defaults, not each arm's settings (e.g. ab-stagger shows FOLD_POLICY empty).

LABELLED CONCURRENCY IS NOT SERVED CONCURRENCY: rounds 1-5 and gpu-suite 'c512' ran at most 186 (round 1, 560 slots, radix on) or 128 (384 slots) requests (server logs 'max_running_requests is capped to 186/128'); round-1 LeapQuant ran with KV 80,348 tokens (mem fraction 0.60, max 144 running). In round 10 fp32 at aa1k c256/c512 ran at most 248 and at ix8k1k c64-c256 at most 53-54 (KV-bound), bf16 window 100-101, LeapQuant 108; at round13 'c1024' bf16 ran at most 724, LeapQuant 929 (not 'all 1,024 running' as summary.txt:963 says), fp32 560.

SINGLE REPETITION: every point from round 10 on is n=1 (only round 9 has r1/r2; gpu-suite LQ has a second repetition). DECISIONS.md asks paired repetitions; two-session means for rounds 12/12b and 13/13b (1.274/1.410/1.454; 1.533/1.060) exist only in summary.txt. round13b c512 LQ/bf16 = 0.983 vs 1.046 in round13 shows the session spread.

REPORTS HIDE SESSIONS: reports/round12b_20261114-0657 (from round12b + round12) and round13b_20261114-0943 (from round13b + round13 + round13-stagger) use identical file names, so only round12b / round13b rows are shown; round13-stagger's LeapQuant arm (same file names as the aligned arm) appears in no snapshot report.

REPORT HEADINGS DO NOT MATCH THE SERVERS: every radix-off paired table is titled 'both servers 560 state slots, up to 512 running' (hard-coded in generate_reports.paired_section), also for round13/13b where bf16 and LeapQuant had 1,100 slots, fp32 560, and up to 1,024 running (mem fraction 0.75).

METHOD/SETTINGS CHANGE ACROSS 'ROUNDS': slots 560 (round 1, radix on) -> 384 (rounds 2-5) -> 560 radix off (6+) -> 1,100/1,310/1,560 radix on; shapes random-length short/long (range ratio 0.0) vs exact decode/aa1k/ix8k1k; prompts per point = 4c (short/long), 2c (decode), c (decode2k), max(2c, 8) (aa1k/ix8k1k: c1 and c4 points have only 8 requests). Cross-round curves are not like for like.

NO JSON RESULTS: all serving logs have output_file=None (the --output-file .jsonl option was added to runbook/env.sh at 22:45 UTC, after every run), so only the rounded text block exists; per-request timings were never saved.

RUNBOOKS NO LONGER REPRODUCE THE RUNS: since 13:55 UTC serving_round9.sh / serving_round10.sh / serving_openloop.sh default LEAPQUANT_DECODE_BACKEND=cuda and kernel/leapquant_engine.py defaults step reuse on; rounds 9/10, openloop, round9-equalmem, sglang-best ran Triton decode with per-layer inputs and builds that no longer exist in the repository (fold library swapped in place).

problems: Only round 10 (3 arms) and round 11 (2 arms) are real concurrency sweeps; round 11 dropped aa1k c4/c128 and ix8k1k c1/c16/c64 but its snapshot report fills them with round 10's rows under the same labels (different LeapQuant binary), so the round-11 'sweep' curve mixes two sessions. serving_ab_step has aa1k 1,4,64,512 only; round12/12b decode 128,256,512; round13/13b decode 512,1024; all others are 1-2 points per shape.

No point beyond c512 for ix8k1k/aa1k and no c512 for ix8k1k at all (DECISIONS.md says 1-256 for InferenceX); decode c1024 exists only in round13/13b/13-stagger with different slot counts (fp32 560, others 1,100).

x axis = client max_concurrency, not served concurrency (server '#running-req' maxima per point): round10 fp32 248 at aa1k c256/c512 and 53-54 at ix8k1k c64-c256; bf16 window 464 (aa1k c512) and 100-101 (ix c128/c256); LeapQuant 497 and 108; round13 c1024: 724 / 929 / 560. Above these knees the curves measure queueing (TTFT), not throughput at that concurrency. Client 'Peak concurrent requests' (e.g. 976-1009 at c512) is a one-second-window count and exceeds the limit.
Tiny samples at low concurrency: aa1k/ix8k1k c1 and c4 use 8 requests (max(2c, 8)), c16 32 requests; one repetition everywhere from round 10 on.

Shapes differ by round: rounds 1-6 'short'/'long' use random lengths (random_range_ratio 0.0, mean ~half the maximum) while decode/aa1k/ix8k1k are exact (1.0); the snapshot paired tables label them, the older config pages do not.

Snapshot charts: only round10 (img/paired_sweep_off_aa1k.png, _ix8k1k.png), openloop (copied round10 sweep images) and round11 have sweep charts; the openloop report re-plots round 10's sweep because it was generated with --with results/round10.

values.label: bf16 window state allocated per entry in the server (ssm_state + ReplaySSM ring d/k/g)

problems: SLOT LABELS DO NOT MATCH THE SERVER LOGS: the snapshot paired tables of round9-equalmem_20261114-0503, radix-equalmem-final_20261114-0956, ab-trackflush_20261114-1129 and ab-slotcopy_20261114-1130 are titled 'Radix cache on: ... (bf16 1,100, LeapQuant 1,560)' (hard-coded in generate_reports.paired_section) while those servers had LeapQuant 1,310 slots ('max_mamba_cache_size: 1310', 'LeapQuant decode state allocated: 24 layers x 1311 slots', capped to 436 running); the same reports' index.html step tables say '1310 slots'. Radix-off titles say '560 state slots, up to 512 running' also for round13/13b (1,100 slots, up to 1,024).
SLOT COUNT OFF BY ONE: LeapQuant allocates configured+1 slots (padding slot): 561 / 1,101 / 1,311 / 1,561 in the logs vs 560 / 1,100 / 1,310 / 1,560 configured.

'EQUAL MEMORY' IS EQUAL ssm_state vs LeapQuant decode state ONLY: bf16 window 1,100 slots = ssm_state 25.80 GiB but also ReplaySSM ring buffers d 3.226 + k 1.613 + g 0.050 = 4.89 GiB and conv 1.21 GiB; LeapQuant 1,310 = 25.956 GiB + conv 1.44 + ssm 0.09. Measured device peaks in the 'equal memory' runs: bf16 window 71,334-71,882 MiB vs LeapQuant 67,028-67,456 MiB (round9-equalmem, radix-equalmem-final .mem): LeapQuant used ~4.3 GiB less, so the runs are not equal-total-memory; KV tokens 492,156 vs 479,653.

THE *_memory.txt EXTRACTS OMIT THE ReplaySSM RING LINE, so any memory figure built from them misses 2.49 GiB (560 slots) / 4.89 GiB (1,100) of bf16-window state and the fp32-window ring (v6/v7: available_gpu_mem 10.38 vs 15.34 GB for fp32 packed).

BYTES PER ENTRY 1.19 vs 2 IS REPLAY ACCOUNTING, NOT SERVER MEMORY: 1.19 = 19,456-byte boundary state per 128x128 head (no window records); the server allocates 11.107 GiB for 561 slots = 1.69 B/entry (window records included, kernel/leapquant_engine.py bytes_allocated) while bf16 window allocates 2.00 (ssm) + 0.38 (ring) = 2.38 B/entry: measured ratio ~1.41x, not 2/1.19 = 1.68x. bf16's 2.00 is a hard-coded constant in kernel/ablation_table.py.

MISSING GPU FIELDS: .mem files exist only from round 10 on (B17); none for rounds 1-9, gpu-suite, v6-v8, openloop/openloop-final(-2,-3) (serving_openloop.sh does not sample memory), prefill-radix, retraction. A .mem holds only the device-wide peak of nvidia-smi memory.used (0.5 s sampling) and the total: no per-process, allocated vs reserved, KV/state split, time series (samples deleted, one leftover file) or clocks/power.

MEMORY ACCOUNTING: the LeapQuant state is allocated after SGLang's 'Memory pool end' (outside --mem-fraction-static; env.sh comment) and mem_usage_bytes() charges only BOUNDARY_FIELDS; SGLang's int8 checkpoint pool (sglang-best-3: 15.61 GB) is also outside the static fraction. KV-token counts therefore are the only like-for-like capacity figure.

NOT IN THE SNAPSHOT: no snapshot report shows GB, KV tokens or .mem peaks (the 11:30 generator never read .mem/server memory lines; the post-snapshot generator of 22:45 UTC does). A memory graphic from reports.zip can only have used headings ('1,100 / 1,560 / 560'), index step descriptions ('1310 slots'), accuracy.html's '1.19 bytes per entry instead of 2' and prose.
prose_only: summary.txt:71-75 '560 fp32 slots are 26.3 GB', '1,536 slots = 72 GB', 'bf16 would need 36 GB', 'LeapQuant slots are 15 MB, not 47' (computed; 15 MB not matching the 21.3 MB/slot in the logs).
summary.txt:197 'phase 1 adds 21 MB/slot'; :288 '21.3 MB instead of 50.3 MB fp32' (computable from logs: 11.107 GiB/561 = 21.3 MB).
summary.txt:309 / run-quick-einstein-v6/NOTES.txt 'LeapQuant 11.1 GB -> 993,215 (2.0x fp32)' (2.0x = KV-token ratio, computed).

summary.txt:773-777 'bf16 window 1,100 slots (25.8 GB ...) against LeapQuant 1,310 slots (25.96 GB ...)': raw lines exist, the 'equal memory' interpretation is prose only and excludes the 4.89 GiB ring.

summary.txt:822-828, 849-853 SGLang int8 checkpoint sizes '2,200 slots, 28.6 GB at 1,100', 'weights 17.6 + state 27 + checkpoints 28.6 GB' for sglang-best-2 (its server never started; no allocation line).
summary.txt:1107 / 22:39 UTC accuracy-strict 'KV 1,388,839 tokens (42.4 GB) ... LeapQuant 0.495 GB': results/accuracy-strict (post-snapshot).

problems: SLO MISSING FROM THE FIGURE: the snapshot open-loop section (reports/openloop_20261114-0413, openloop-final_20261114-0815) says only 'goodput counts the requests that met the SLO'; the thresholds (TTFT <= 2,000 ms, TPOT <= 50 ms) are recorded only in each log's benchmark_args (goodput=[('ttft', 2000.0), ('tpot', 50.0)]), runbook/serving_openloop.sh and docs/DECISIONS.md.

SLO DIFFERS FROM THE DECLARED ONE: DECISIONS.md's Service SLO also requires p99 time between tokens <= 100 ms; goodput ignores it. Measured p99 ITL is 115-296 ms for both arms at every rate >= 6 req/s (and 97/98 ms for LeapQuant at 4), so under the declared SLO neither server meets it from 6 req/s on. Per-request timings were not saved (output_details=False), so goodput cannot be recomputed with another SLO.

FIGURE MIXES EXPERIMENTS: reports/openloop-final_20261114-0815 was generated from results/openloop-final + results/openloop; same file names hide each other, so rates 2 and 4 (all arms) and the whole 'own step' arm come from results/openloop (11:20-12:12 UTC: build_v6 batched-GS ae3affd2, Triton decode, no step reuse) while rates 6-12 of bf16/aligned come from openloop-final (15:49 UTC: build_v9, CUDA decode v9, step reuse). The table does not mark the session. reports/openloop_20261114-0413 also embeds round 10's closed-loop sweep (generated --with results/round10).

COMPLETION RATE IS 100% EVERYWHERE: all 42 open-loop logs report 'Successful requests: 600' of 600; the 'Completed, req/s' column is request throughput (600 / benchmark duration, which includes the drain after the last arrival), so it saturates near 6 req/s for both arms and is not an offered-vs-completed rate.

REPETITIONS: rates 8/9/10 have three sessions (openloop-final, -2, -3); rates 6, 11, 12 one session with the final build; rates 2, 4 and the own-step arm only the old build. All sessions use --seed 1 (identical arrival times and prompts in every session and arm), so the three-session 95% interval in summary.txt:965-970 reflects server run-to-run noise only.

CAPACITY BOUNDARY IS KV-BOUND: at >= 10 req/s bf16 window peaks at 464 running and LeapQuant at 497 (server logs; KV 926,316 vs 993,215 tokens / 2,000 tokens per request); the goodput gap above the boundary partly reflects KV room, not only kernel speed. 'At the capacity boundary' has no rate in DECISIONS.md: the gate is met at 10 req/s, not at 9 (summary.txt:970).

BUILD LABELS: arm names (bf16_window, leapquant_aligned) are identical across sessions with different LeapQuant binaries; openloop's server log has no 'LeapQuant decode:' line (Triton decode) - only manifests tell them apart.

problems: STAGGER COMPARISONS ARE CROSS-SESSION: results/round13-stagger ran only the LeapQuant arm (STATUS: 'S1 ... skipped: bf16 window in results/round13', 'U1 ... skipped: fp32 in results/round13'), 30-40 min after round 13; summary.txt:972-976 sets its p99 ITL (48.1 / 83.6 ms) beside round 13's bf16/fp32/aligned (52.7/64.6/69.8 at c512; 77.1/75.1/119.5 at c1024).

STAGGER ARM IS UNLABELLED: round13-stagger's files are named serving_off_leapquant_cuda_r1_* exactly like round 13's aligned arm; only manifest.txt (LEAPQUANT_FOLD_POLICY=stagger) records the policy. reports/round13b_20261114-0943 lists results/round13-stagger as a source but its rows are hidden by round13b's same-named files: no snapshot report shows the stagger numbers.

SNAPSHOT A/B REPORTS HAVE NO PAIRED TABLE: ab-stagger, ab-trackflush, ab-slotcopy labels (lq_policy_*, lq_auto/aligned/stagger, lq_field/fused) do not match generate_reports.PAIRED_LABEL, so their paired tables are all dashes; the p99 values exist only in the raw 'Full measurements' table and in prose.

p99 ITL IS POOLED OVER ALL TOKEN GAPS OF ALL REQUESTS (SGLang bench), one run per point; ab-policy's default arm and ab-stagger's default arm differ by <1 ms, but no repetition exists for any stagger/track-flush/slot-copy arm.

p99 TTFT IN CLOSED LOOP IS QUEUEING: with prompts = 2c and the server capped (464-497 running at aa1k c512; 366/436 radix-on), p99 TTFT (~68-69 s at aa1k c512, 18-23 s at radix-on decode c512, 101-110 s at decode2k) is the second wave waiting for slots/KV, not prefill latency; comparing p99 TTFT across arms with different running caps compares admission limits.

RADIX ON/OFF COMPARISONS MIX BUILDS AND SLOT COUNTS: radix-align0 (ALIGN_FOLDS=0, 1,560 slots, build_v9) vs sglang-best-3 LeapQuant (aligned, 1,560) are back-to-back but different sessions; round 9 on/off used 1,100/1,560 slots and the pre-v3 fold; summary.txt:864 compares radix-align0 with round9-equalmem (1,310 slots, build_v6 Triton decode, 'another session').

SLO LINE: DECISIONS.md's 100 ms p99-ITL SLO is drawn only in prose; LeapQuant aligned exceeds it at round13 c1024 (119.5 / 118.8 ms) and in radix-on short c512 (107-176 ms) - bf16 window too at round9 off short c512 (150.6 / 156.7 ms).

SUMMARY.txt: grep of 'bit-identical' and 'RESULT' lines / table 'trace, bit-identical folds, criterion C, result'.

problems: NORM NOT STATED: every 'output error' is a pooled relative L2 (Frobenius) norm, 100*sqrt(sum_t sum_h ||y-y_fp32||^2 / sum_t sum_h ||y_fp32||^2) over all tokens x heads x 128 values of ONE layer's recurrent-kernel output (not the model output/logits, not a mean of per-token errors, so dominated by large-norm tokens/heads). It is defined only in code (leapquant_replay.cpp l.444-447/567, reference_heads.cpp length_of = sqrt(sum of squares), verify_kernel.py l.407-409/500-501, engine tests). Reports/docs say only 'distance from the fp32 result, as a share of its size' / 'all heads and all tokens together'; verify_free_run.png and accuracy_*.png carry no norm, pooling or token-count definition.

DIFFERENT QUANTITIES UNDER ONE NAME: replay output error (vs fp32 replay), verify C (vs fp32 truth heads, free run), verify A (kernel vs reference core, per token-head, floored), verify B (fold/state reconstruction loss, not output), and set C / F99 numbers (0.952, 0.827-0.861, 2.387) which are geometric means of kernel/reference RATIOS, not errors. 'Reference' in verification charts means the CPU LeapQuant reference core, not fp32 and not bf16.

LEAPQUANT DEFINITION CHANGES BETWEEN EXPERIMENTS: reference core with sequential fit 8 sweeps (creative-franklin c_replay; v4 s20_rank8), sequential 2 sweeps (v4/v5 c_replay, gpu-suite d_verify references, S21), joint fit 2 sweeps (s20_ablations base, layer_map, every verify reference from fast_checks on). Same trace, different 'LeapQuant': explain L13 0.727% (seq) vs 1.108% (joint); explain L30 1.605 vs 1.738; all_layers L0 0.007 (S21) vs 0.013 (layer_map); rank 8 explain L30 0.757 (8 sw seq) / 0.883 (2 sw seq) / 1.050 (2 sw joint). All are labelled 'LeapQuant (1.19 bytes/entry)'.

SAME TRACE NAMES, DIFFERENT RECORDINGS: creative-franklin traces (old host) vs quick-einstein traces re-recorded 13 Nov 11:21-11:35 PST; bf16-window errors differ (code L0 0.741 vs 0.491, explain L0 0.558 vs 0.956, reasoning L0 0.381 vs 1.233). summary.txt lines 21-24 and reports/accuracy.html use the old set, all later pages the new set. The all_layers set is a third, separate recording of the reasoning prompt (state error after 1,024 tokens differs from traces/reasoning). No trace .bin is in the repository (they live on the GPU host; the old host's are gone), so values can be re-parsed, not recomputed.

MIXED TRACE SETS/LENGTHS: 9 prompt traces at 4,095 tokens vs 24 all-layer traces at 2,047 tokens (prose says 2,048) vs S18 at 1,600 tokens vs synthetic 400 tokens (README 0.8537%). F99's 33-trace geometric mean counts the reasoning prompt 27 times (its layers 0/13/30 twice from two recordings) and code/explain 3 times each.

FIGURES THAT MIX EXPERIMENTS: verify_free_run.png / verification.html in reports v7_20261113-2250, -2304 and v8-radix combine gpu-suite d_verify (exact kernel, sequential-fit reference) with fast_checks_v2 verify (Triton, joint-fit reference): the 'Reference core (CPU)' bar for explain L13 is 0.7268% in one row and 1.1078% in another. round9_20261114-0144 combines fast_fold_v1 (CUDA fold v1, 9 prompt traces) with fast_checks_final (Triton fold, 24 all-layer traces), both labelled '(fast kernels)'. round10_20261114-0309 shows fast_decode_v5 (CUDA decode v5, NOT adopted; round 10 served Triton decode + build_v6 fold, which has no 9-trace verify). The identical accuracy+verification rows are republished in three reports (v7_2250, v7_2304, v8-radix).

WRONG SOURCE LABELS AND MIXED FIT IN ONE PAGE: pages print 'Source: c_replay_*.txt' / 'Source: d_verify_*.txt' while the data are s20_ablations/base_*.txt and verify_*.txt. v7/v8 accuracy pages add an 'Eight compensators on layer 30' table that lists all 9 traces from gpu-suite s20_rank8 (sequential, 2 sweeps) next to joint-fit base charts; v5's version of that table is 8 sweeps.
